result.text:
Larsson Distributors AB, a Gothenburg-based pharma distributor, is showing consistent slippage in payment behaviour. It has 4 open invoices with client CL03 totalling roughly €202.8k against a €270k credit limit, of which one (INV001137 at €69.2k) is 25 days past due, with three more due shortly. Settled history shows lateness worsening from 13 to 20 days on the last two paid invoices, and the current overdue item continues that pattern; the payment review records the trend as deteriorating. Separately, Trade Ledger reported on 20 September 2026 that multiple suppliers say the company has fallen behind on scheduled payments over the past quarter, a severity 4 unpaid_vendors item logged directly against the entity rather than via a parent.

The buyer scores 37.3 and sits in the Watch band, driven by 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD, worst line CL03) + 0.35 x 44.6 (news) = 37.3, giving a PD of 0.2727. Payment contributes a weighted 21.7 and news a weighted 15.6. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the band is well supported because both streams point the same way, but the score sits close to the 35 threshold and leans heavily on a single article whose body is one sentence, with no named vendors, no amounts, no timeframe detail and no company response, carried by one publication with no corroborating source. The item has decayed only from base 45 to 44.57 at 5 days, so as it ages the score trends toward the payment-only weighted 21.7 and the buyer would fall below 35 into Healthy with no genuine improvement. The review also notes the payment raw of 33.3 is a point-in-time reading that does not capture the worsening direction, and that the two streams measure the same underlying behaviour and should not be read as two separate risk drivers.

The recommendation for Solvenza Trade Credit (CL03, LIM0029) is REDUCE: cut the current limit of 270000 to a revised 247525, set at the point where expected loss meets the 25% appetite. Expected loss falls from 53197 to 48769 against a PD of 0.2727 versus a PD target of 0.25; the maximum liability constraint does not bind. The underwriter should also note the review's point that €202.8k of exposure is 75% of the €270k limit, leaving limited headroom if further invoices go overdue, and that the limit was last reviewed in Aug 2024 and should be re-underwritten rather than relied on.

An upgrade should rest on payment evidence, not on the news item decaying. What would lift the band is the €69.2k overdue INV001137 being cleared and the three invoices due shortly being settled on time, reversing the slippage from 13 to 20 to 25 days and restoring headroom under the limit. Corroboration or refutation of the Trade Ledger report, whether named vendors, amounts, a timeframe, a company response or a second publication, would firm up or remove the weighted 15.6 news contribution that the adjudicator identifies as the least robust part of the score. Given the deteriorating trend, the adjudicator's stance is a firm Watch with a downgrade bias rather than a borderline case likely to self-resolve.
